events.headline: Democrats Retake Senate and House in US Midterms; Bottoms Wins Georgia Governor's Race
events.summary: Democrats flipped control of both the US Senate (net gain of at least four seats) and House (projected 245+ seats) in the November 3 midterm elections. Keisha Lance Bottoms defeated Rick Jackson 54.3%-45.7% to become Georgia's first Black woman governor, the first Democratic governor there since 1998.

events.headline: UN Confirms Receipt of Haiti Gang Leader's Peace Letter as El Salvador Deploys 2,000+ Troops
events.summary: The United Nations confirmed it received a mediation letter from a Haitian gang leader proposing talks, as El Salvador committed more than 2,000 troops to support Haiti's security mission. Missing Salvadoran soldiers referenced by the gang leader are now effectively presumed dead.

events.headline: Urda Rail Crash Probe Focuses on Signal-Override Order From Madrid Control Centre
events.summary: Investigators probing the Oct 28 high-speed rail collision near Urda (at least 68-69 killed) say that after a computer failure disabled the automatic safety system, an operator at Adif's Madrid-Atocha control centre told the AVE driver to resume normal running despite a red signal, even though the other train had reported it was still stopped on the track. Spain's rail accident authority has widened the investigation.

events.headline: DR Congo Ebola Outbreak Tops 10,400 Cases With Case-Fatality Rate Above 50%, Spread Confirmed Abroad
events.summary: The outbreak, centered in Ituri Province, has reached 10,445 cumulative cases and 5,372 deaths in DRC, a case-fatality rate near 51-52%, making it the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in DRC history. Confirmed cases also reported in Kenya, Uganda (including Kampala), Nigeria, and an imported case in France.

events.headline: Polish President Nawrocki Confronts Judges as Riot Police Deployed in Court Standoff
events.summary: Poland's constitutional crisis escalated as President Karol Nawrocki had a physical confrontation with judges at the Constitutional Tribunal, prompting deployment of riot police. The standoff between Nawrocki and the Tusk government has already triggered the resignation of three Polish ambassadors.

events.headline: Al-Shabaab Claims Mass-Casualty Ambush on Somali Convoy in Lower Shabelle
events.summary: On Oct 26-27, 2026, al-Shabaab ambushed a Somali government/allied-militia convoy near Leego, Lower Shabelle region, during Operation Banooda, using explosive-laden vehicles; al-Shabaab claims it killed over 300 troops, while Somali officials counter it was a major assault by government forces. The death toll is independently unconfirmed, but analysts call it the army's worst setback since 2023.

events.headline: Russian Bombing of Aid Site and Shelter in Komyshuvakha Kills At Least 26
events.summary: Russian forces bombed a school used as a humanitarian aid distribution point in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia Oblast, on Nov 2, then struck a shelter where residents had fled with roughly nine more bombs. The death toll rose through the day to at least 26, with dozens still missing; President Zelensky called the attack 'exceptionally horrific' and declared a day of mourning.

events.headline: Mandatory Evacuations in Pagosa Springs, Colorado, as San Juan River Nears Record Crest
events.summary: A second storm wave triggered mandatory evacuations in Archuleta County, Colorado, as the San Juan River rose to 16.8 feet/11,200 cfs — the second-highest stage on record, just below the historic 1911 mark of 17.8 feet. Highway 160 closed, Red Cross shelters opened, and the Colorado National Guard deployed.

events.headline: Federal Judge Rejects DOJ Bid to Segregate About 20,000 'Likely Non-Citizen' California Ballots
events.summary: A federal judge denied a DOJ emergency request to force California to segregate roughly 20,000 ballots the department claims belong to likely non-citizens, two days before the Nov. 3 election, ruling it would "wreak havoc" on the vote. An appeals panel also rejected a similar request.

events.headline: US to Host Russia-Ukraine Trilateral Talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov 10-11
events.summary: US officials Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will lead trilateral talks with Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi on Nov 10-11, reviving a diplomatic track on post-war security arrangements that had been suspended since February.

events.headline: Texas Flips: Democrat Gina Hinojosa Elected Governor, Ousting Greg Abbott
events.summary: Democratic state Rep. Gina Hinojosa defeated incumbent Gov. Greg Abbott, becoming Texas's first Democratic governor since the 1990s and its first Hispanic governor. The same night, Democrat James Talarico defeated Sen. Ken Paxton for US Senate, Texas's first Democratic Senate win since 1988, and Vikki Goodwin unseated 10-year incumbent Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick.

events.headline: Coordinated Attacks Across Tolima, Huila and Cauca Kill at Least Seven in Colombia
events.summary: A wave of coordinated bombings and armed attacks hit multiple Colombian departments including Tolima, Huila and Cauca, killing at least seven people, including an infant, and wounding more than 20. The attacks expand on an earlier truck-bomb and drone strike near a military base in Planadas, Tolima, pointing to a broader coordinated campaign.

events.headline: UN Investigation Finds Hallmarks of Genocide in El Fasher One Year After RSF Takeover
events.summary: A UN fact-finding mission concluded that mass killings, gang rapes and deliberate starvation by the RSF in El Fasher, North Darfur, constitute "the hallmarks of genocide." One year after the city's October 2025 capture, North Darfur's governor alleges RSF forces committed 320 gang-rape cases at El Fasher University and 140 mass graves have been identified; Amnesty International's October 2026 follow-up found ongoing unlawful killings, detention, starvation and torture of civilians.

events.headline: US Carries Out Limited Strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island Near Strait of Hormuz
events.summary: The US military conducted limited 'defensive' strikes on targets on Iran's Qeshm Island on Nov 2-3, officials said, aimed at countering Iranian surface-to-air missile systems threatening shipping near the Strait of Hormuz. Officials stressed the action does not represent a resumption of major combat operations.

events.headline: Nearly 6 Million Face Acute Hunger in Haiti Amid Gang Violence and El Nino Drought
events.summary: The UN estimates nearly 5.94 million Haitians face acute food insecurity, a figure projected to rise to 6.35 million by mid-2027, driven by gang violence and El Nino-linked drought. Separately, the UN human rights office reports more than 5,700 people killed or wounded by gang violence between January and mid-September, including over 1,000 rapes and 230 kidnappings.

events.headline: Historic Flash Flooding Triggers Mass Evacuations in Sedona, Arizona
events.summary: A second Pacific storm dumped up to 4 inches of rain across the Southwest on Nov. 1-2, triggering mandatory evacuations in Sedona zones near Oak Creek and prompting water rescues. The same system caused severe flooding in southern Colorado, where Gov. Polis issued a disaster declaration.

events.headline: Palisades Fire Arson Retrial Begins in Los Angeles Federal Court
events.summary: Jury selection began Nov. 2 in the federal retrial of Jonathan Rinderknecht, who is accused of igniting the Palisades Fire. His first trial ended in a hung jury in June 2026.

events.headline: Learjet Crashes Near Greenacres, Florida, Killing All 9 Aboard
events.summary: A Learjet 60 flying from Austin, Texas, to North Eleuthera, Bahamas, crashed near a residential area in Greenacres, Florida, around 12:50 p.m. on Nov. 1, killing all nine people aboard. Gov. Ron DeSantis called the crash "cataclysmic."

events.headline: RSF Drone Strikes Push Sudan's Power Grid Toward Collapse
events.summary: Rapid Support Forces drones have struck 15-18 power stations across Sudan since early October, including the 500-megawatt Um Dabakir plant on Oct 29, cutting White Nile and North Kordofan states off the national grid. The campaign threatens to collapse what remains of Sudan's electricity infrastructure amid the ongoing civil war.

events.headline: Oregon's 2026 Wildfire Season Becomes Largest on Record, Nearly 2 Million Acres Burned
events.summary: Oregon's 2026 wildfire season burned roughly 2 to 2.3 million acres, surpassing the prior record of about 1.93 million acres set in 2024, at a suppression cost near $1.4 billion. FEMA reversed an earlier denial of federal fire-management assistance for the Rowe Creek Complex fire after appeals from Oregon lawmakers.

events.headline: Deb Haaland Elected New Mexico Governor, First Native American Woman to Lead a US State
events.summary: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland defeated Republican Rio Rancho Mayor Gregg Hull by roughly 57%-43% to become New Mexico's governor. Haaland is the first Native American woman elected to lead any US state.

events.headline: US Military Boat-Strike Campaign Continues; Cumulative Drug-Boat Death Toll Tops 240
events.summary: The US military carried out additional strikes on suspected drug-smuggling boats in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific, pushing the cumulative death toll from the campaign past 240. The strikes continue a controversial campaign that has drawn criticism over its legality and lack of transparency.

events.headline: UN Rapporteur Calls Myanmar's Human Rights Situation 'Catastrophic' Amid Junta Attacks on Civilians
events.summary: A UN Special Rapporteur described Myanmar's human rights situation as catastrophic, saying the junta is attacking civilians to terrorize them while continuing arms purchases to fuel the war. The statement follows junta airstrikes that killed children at a school in Karenni State and bombed villages in Rakhine.

events.headline: Indonesia Detains Three Police Generals Over Alleged Wiretapping of President Prabowo
events.summary: Indonesian authorities detained three police generals suspected of illegally wiretapping President Prabowo Subianto. The case has raised questions about internal security and loyalty within Indonesia's police force.

events.headline: Pakistan Launches Counter-Strikes on Afghan Taliban Border Posts in South Waziristan
events.summary: Pakistani forces struck Afghan Taliban border posts in South Waziristan in response to what officials called unprovoked cross-border firing. The clash escalates tensions beyond the diplomatic track, even as Pakistan continues pressing the Taliban over the TTP with US mediation offered.

events.headline: Israeli Forces Kill Additional Palestinians in Khan Younis Despite Gaza Ceasefire
events.summary: Israeli forces killed at least four Palestinians in Khan Younis and al-Mawasi, with a fifth later dying of wounds, despite a nominal ceasefire in Gaza. The killings follow a similar incident the previous day that killed eight Palestinians, including police officers and a child.

events.headline: RBA Raises Cash Rate to 4.85%, Highest Since 2008
events.summary: Australia's central bank raised its cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.85% on Nov 3 in a 6-3 board vote, the fifth hike of 2026, citing annual inflation at 3.7% and spillover effects from Middle East oil-price volatility.

events.headline: Poland Says It Blocked Overnight Sabotage Provocation Near Kaliningrad Border
events.summary: Polish authorities said they blocked an overnight provocation involving individuals using flashlights near the border with Russia's Kaliningrad exclave, who withdrew before being intercepted. The incident follows Poland's deployment of counter-terrorism police to the region over sabotage warnings.

events.headline: US Moves to Remove South Africa and Rwanda From AGOA Trade Program
events.summary: The Trump administration notified Congress of its intent to terminate South Africa's and Rwanda's participation in the African Growth and Opportunity Act trade program. South Africa said it would challenge the decision.

events.headline: China Conducts Record Surge in Military Activity Around Taiwan
events.summary: Taiwan's defense ministry reported a record daily surge in Chinese military activity around the island, including 49 aircraft, six warships and six government vessels. The surge marks one of the largest single-day shows of force in recent months.

events.headline: Rubio Hosts Venezuelan FM Blanco, Reaffirms Three-Phase Transition Plan
events.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Venezuela's new Foreign Minister Oliver Blanco on Nov 2, reaffirming a three-phase stabilization, economic-recovery and democratic-transition plan for Venezuela. Rubio urged the release of political prisoners, with Foro Penal counting 344 currently detained.

events.headline: China's CXMT Completes Validation of Next-Generation 4F2 DRAM Chip
events.summary: Chinese memory maker CXMT completed engineering-sample verification of its sixth-generation 4F2-architecture DRAM chip in early November, targeting DDR5 server modules by year-end. The breakthrough intensifies competition with Samsung and SK Hynix amid a global chip market selloff.

events.headline: EUFOR Chinook Helicopter Crash Near Brčko, Bosnia and Herzegovina Kills Four
events.summary: An Italian military Chinook helicopter serving with the EU peacekeeping force EUFOR crashed near Brčko, Bosnia and Herzegovina, killing four crew members. The cause of the crash is under investigation.

events.headline: South Korea's Kospi Plunges Over 3% as Chip Stocks Tumble on AI Valuation Fears
events.summary: South Korea's Kospi index fell roughly 3-3.6% on Nov 3, with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix shares dropping 4.6-5.1%, amid a broader US tech selloff driven by doubts over AI infrastructure spending.

events.headline: Sen. Chris Murphy Hospitalized After Suffering Stroke in Connecticut
events.summary: Sen. Chris Murphy, 53, experienced arm numbness on Nov. 1 at his son's hockey game in Connecticut and was taken to a local hospital, where doctors determined he'd had a stroke. He was transferred to Johns Hopkins in Baltimore for monitoring; his office says he is awake, alert, and expected to make a full recovery.

events.headline: Kansas Elects First Democratic US Senator Since 1932; Governor's Race Still Undecided
events.summary: Democrat Adam Hamilton defeated incumbent Republican Sen. Roger Marshall in Kansas's most expensive race in state history, about $110 million. The governor's race between Democrat Cindy Holscher and Republican Ty Masterson remains too close to call with about 98% counted, while Democrat Chris Mann has declared victory for attorney general over incumbent Kris Kobach, who has not conceded.

events.headline: Josh Shapiro Re-elected Pennsylvania Governor in Landslide Over Stacy Garrity
events.summary: Gov. Josh Shapiro (D) defeated Republican state Treasurer Stacy Garrity by a wide margin, roughly 60%-37%, despite a Trump endorsement for Garrity. The decisive win cements Shapiro as a prominent national Democratic figure heading into his second term.

events.headline: Nationwide 'GenZ Regelt' Protests in Germany Turn Violent
events.summary: Tens of thousands protested cost-of-living, education and budget-cut policies across German cities on Oct 31-Nov 1, with clashes in Frankfurt, Berlin, Hamburg and Cologne. Police used water cannon and pepper spray after Molotov cocktails were thrown and shops were looted; officials blamed 'infiltrators' for the violence.

events.headline: Xavier Becerra Elected California Governor, First Latino Governor in Over 150 Years
events.summary: Democrat Xavier Becerra defeated Republican Steve Hilton by a wide margin, roughly 64%-36%, to become California's next governor. Becerra is the state's first Latino governor in more than 150 years.

events.headline: North Korea Fires Multiple Missiles Toward East Sea From Sondok Area
events.summary: North Korea fired several missiles toward the East Sea from the Sondok area in South Hamgyong Province, marking its fourth such launch in a month. Pyongyang denied separate US claims linking it to a cryptocurrency exchange hack.
events.locationName: Sondok, South Hamgyong Province, North Korea

events.headline: Thousands Rally in New Delhi Demanding Resignation of India's Election Chief
events.summary: Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi led a rally in New Delhi on Nov 1 demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a voter-roll revision that purged more than 130 million names. The opposition alleges the revision disproportionately benefits the ruling BJP.

events.headline: Prescott, Arizona Declares State of Emergency After Flooding Overtops Watson Lake Dam
events.summary: Prescott's mayor declared a state of emergency after heavy rainfall overtopped the Watson Lake (Granite) Dam, with inflow peaking above 4,000 cfs; the Upper Goldwater Reservoir also topped. The dam is rated to safely handle up to 10 feet of overtopping; low-water crossings closed.

events.headline: One Year After Typhoon Halong, Kipnuk and Kwigillingok Villages Remain in Limbo Amid FEMA Relocation Dispute
events.summary: A year after the remnants of Typhoon Halong destroyed over 150 homes and forced roughly 1,500 evacuations in the Yup'ik villages of Kipnuk and Kwigillingok, Alaska, most residents remain displaced. Both villages voted to relocate entirely, but the state's FEMA request to fund permanent replacement housing for 219 damaged homes has been denied, and temporary housing assistance is set to expire in April 2027.

events.headline: Ukrainian Drones Strike Russia's Slavneft-YANOS Oil Refinery in Yaroslavl
events.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the Slavneft-YANOS oil refinery in Yaroslavl, Russia, triggering fires and power outages felt as far as occupied Crimea. The attack is part of Ukraine's intensified campaign against Russian energy infrastructure.

events.headline: PAHO Warns of Dengue and Chikungunya Resurgence Across the Americas
events.summary: The Pan American Health Organization reports 1.69 million suspected dengue cases across the Americas as of mid-September 2026, including 3,413 severe cases and 571 deaths. Chikungunya is also resurging in Guyana, French Guiana, Suriname and Paraguay, prompting a US CDC health advisory.

events.headline: UN Peacekeeping Mission in Western Sahara Ends After 35 Years
events.summary: The UN Security Council failed to renew the mandate of MINURSO, its peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara, triggering a wind-down that began Nov 1 after 35 years of operation.

events.headline: Niger Receives First Algerian Fuel Convoy Under Joint Military Escort
events.summary: Around 53-60 Algerian fuel trucks carrying roughly 1.65 million liters arrived in Agadez, Niger, on Oct 31-Nov 1 under joint military escort, marking Algeria's first troop deployment abroad since 1973.

events.headline: South Africa Holds Nationwide Local Government Elections
events.summary: South Africans vote Nov 4 in local government elections for 10,526 council seats, with special voting held Nov 2-3 and 732 parties registered to contest seats nationwide.

events.headline: Thornton Man Charged With Murder in Fatal Halloween-Night Shooting Near CU Boulder
events.summary: Boulder police arrested 18-year-old Omar Perez of Thornton on Nov. 2, 2026, charging him with first-degree murder, assault and attempted murder in connection with a Halloween-night shooting at a party in Boulder's University Hill neighborhood. The shooting killed 19-year-old CU Boulder student Luca Hanlon and wounded a second student; it is reportedly Boulder's first homicide of 2026.

events.headline: Georgia Ponzi Scheme Founder Brant Frost Sentenced to 15 Years, Ordered to Pay $76.4 Million Restitution
events.summary: Edwin Brant Frost IV, founder of First Liberty Building & Loan in Newnan, Georgia, was sentenced to 15 years in prison and ordered to pay $76.4 million in restitution after pleading guilty to wire fraud in a Ponzi scheme the SEC says defrauded roughly 300 investors of about $140 million. Funds were also funneled to conservative political causes and Alabama politicians.

events.headline: Cartel Violence Kills Seven, Including US Citizen Child, After Gulf Cartel Lieutenant's Arrest
events.summary: Violence erupted in Matamoros, Mexico after the arrest of a senior Gulf Cartel lieutenant, leaving seven people dead including a US citizen child. Mexican authorities deployed roughly 450 additional troops to the border city to restore order.

events.headline: Serbia Detains Senior Police Officials Over Torture and Abuse-of-Office Allegations
events.summary: Serbian authorities detained several senior police officials, including a police chief, on allegations of torture and abuse of office. The arrests come amid continued political turmoil in Serbia following recent elections.

events.headline: Washington Reports Fatal Human H5N1 Bird Flu Case in Yakima County Dairy Worker
events.summary: A Yakima County resident with underlying health conditions died on or around Nov. 1, 2026, after exposure to H5N1-infected dairy cattle, the first US avian influenza death of 2026 and Washington's second fatal avian-flu infection within roughly a year. The Yakima Health District also confirmed a third human case in the county; the outbreak has affected roughly 33 dairy herds in Washington since Oct. 8.

events.headline: Yemeni Government Forces Advance in Al-Jawf Under 'Operation Dawn of Yemen'
events.summary: Yemeni government forces seized strategic positions in Al-Jawf governorate as part of 'Operation Dawn of Yemen,' while the Saudi-led coalition intercepted a Houthi missile amid intensifying fighting. Yemeni forces reported over 1,200 strikes on Houthi positions in 24 hours.

events.headline: Ohio Measles Outbreak Expands to 24 Counties, Cases Nearly 600% Higher Than 2025
events.summary: Ohio has recorded 296 measles cases across 24 counties in 2026 — a roughly 558-600% increase over 2025's 45 cases — in the state's third distinct outbreak of the year, concentrated in Wayne, Geauga, Ashtabula and Medina counties. Officials cite MMR vaccination coverage (88.3%) below the 95% herd-immunity threshold.

events.headline: Democrat Aaron Ford Elected Nevada Governor as Democrats Sweep Statewide Offices
events.summary: Democratic Attorney General Aaron Ford defeated Republican incumbent Gov. Joe Lombardo to become Nevada's first Black governor. Democrats also won lieutenant governor, attorney general and treasurer, and held secretary of state, marking a full statewide sweep for the first time in decades.

events.headline: Whistleblower Alleges Sanctioned Russian Firm Secretly Financed Alaska Gas Project
events.summary: Former Polar LNG CEO Joel Riddle told the New York Times he resigned after discovering Russian energy giant Novatek, partially sanctioned over the Ukraine war, was financing and directing an Alaska North Slope gas export project despite being told funding came from a UAE firm. The allegations could trigger a US Treasury sanctions probe into the Trump-administration-linked deal; Polar LNG calls the claims unfounded and says it is investigating.

events.headline: Virginia Voters Decide Amendments on Felon Voting Rights, Abortion, Same-Sex Marriage
events.summary: Virginia's Nov. 3, 2026 ballot included a constitutional amendment to automatically restore voting rights to people upon release from incarceration, ending the current system requiring individual governor approval. Two companion amendments addressed reproductive rights and marriage equality; all three were referred to voters by the General Assembly.

events.headline: Federal and State Agents Raid Twin Cities Autism Service Providers in Medicaid Fraud Probe
events.summary: State and federal agents, including the FBI, HHS-OIG, and Minnesota's AG Medicaid Fraud Control Unit, executed search warrants in late October 2026 at Iska Inc. in St. Louis Park and Bright Horizon Therapy Center in Edina, two autism-therapy providers accused of large-scale Medicaid overbilling. The raids followed an earlier spring round targeting additional centers, part of a broader multi-count fraud crackdown.

events.headline: Atmospheric River Triggers Flash Flooding, Evacuations in Northern New Mexico and Southeast Utah
events.summary: An atmospheric-river storm triggered severe flash flooding Nov. 1-3, 2026, across northern New Mexico, where the Rio Chama overflowed its banks, forcing evacuation of hundreds of Chama-area residents and closing US-64/84. In southeastern Utah's San Juan County, historic flooding washed out roads including the Comb Wash bridge and prompted shelter-in-place orders in Bluff.

events.headline: LA and Long Beach Port Security Workers' Strike Delayed to Nov. 4 Deadline as Talks Continue
events.summary: Port employers and ILWU Local 26, representing roughly 250 maritime watchmen and security workers, extended their contract negotiation deadline from Nov. 1 to 5 p.m. Pacific on Nov. 4, 2026, temporarily averting a strike. The terminals they guard handle roughly 85% of Long Beach's and 33% of LA's cargo.

events.headline: Brigham and Women's Hospital Nurses Set Open-Ended Strike for Nov. 12 Amid Contract Fight
events.summary: More than 4,000 Brigham and Women's Hospital nurses issued a 10-day notice for an open-ended strike starting Nov. 12 after rejecting Mass General Brigham's "last, best, final" contract offer. Talks resume Nov. 9, three days before the deadline; disputes center on pay, staffing ratios, and insurance choice.

events.headline: Mayor Mamdani Threatens Legal Action Against ICE Over Use of NYC Park Lots as Staging Grounds
events.summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani sent DHS a letter demanding ICE stop using city-owned lots at Van Cortlandt Park (Bronx) and near Flushing Meadows Corona Park (Queens) as enforcement staging areas, calling it unauthorized under his February executive order, and threatening legal action.

events.headline: Widespread Flooding Prompts State of Emergency, School Closures in Okeechobee and Brevard Counties, Florida
events.summary: A slow-moving storm dumped 5-10 inches of rain across Florida Nov. 1-2, flooding roads in Okeechobee County (which declared a state of emergency) and Brevard County (Palm Bay, Titusville, Satellite Beach, Cocoa Beach). Schools in both counties plus Florida Tech closed Monday.

events.headline: Two Teenagers Killed in Halloween-Night Shooting Outside Spartanburg Cook Out
events.summary: A 15-year-old (Jayden Watkins) and a 17-year-old (Shane Dawkins) were shot and killed around 11:30 p.m. Oct. 31 in the parking lot of a Cook Out restaurant in Spartanburg, South Carolina. A third person suffered non-life-threatening injuries; no suspects had been identified as of Nov. 2.

events.headline: Fatal Shooting at Madison Senior High School Youth Football Game in Illinois
events.summary: One adult was killed and three others wounded in a shooting shortly after 10:45 p.m. Nov. 1 at Madison Senior High School in Madison, Illinois (St. Louis metro area) during a youth football league championship game. The school canceled classes Monday and Tuesday, and the Major Case Squad of Greater St. Louis is investigating.

events.headline: Zelensky Visits Berlin for Air-Defense Talks With Chancellor Merz
events.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky traveled to Berlin to meet German Chancellor Friedrich Merz for talks focused on bolstering Ukraine's air-defense capabilities. The visit comes amid continued Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure.

events.headline: Storm Agneta Triggers Severe Flooding in Rhodes, Greece, With Alerts Extending to Spain
events.summary: Storm Agneta brought severe flooding to Rhodes and other parts of Greece, damaging dozens of vehicles, while red-alert weather warnings were also issued in parts of Spain. Authorities warned the storm system would continue moving across the eastern Mediterranean.

events.headline: Utah Legislature Sees Democratic Gains; Ben McAdams Wins Back US House Seat
events.summary: Early results showed roughly 15 Democratic and unaffiliated challengers leading or defeating Republican state legislative incumbents in historically GOP-dominated Utah. Democrat Ben McAdams won Utah's 1st Congressional District, and voters passed Amendment A removing newspaper-publication requirements from the state constitution while rejecting Amendment B, which would have raised the threshold for tax-related ballot initiatives.

events.headline: Pennsylvania Legislature Control at Stake as Democrats Eye First Senate Majority Since 1978
events.summary: Pennsylvania voters elected all 203 state House members and half the 50-seat state Senate on Nov. 3, 2026. Democrats held a narrow 103-100 House majority entering the election and sought to flip four GOP-held Senate seats, which combined with the governorship would create a Democratic trifecta.

events.headline: Ohio Voters Decide Open Governor's Race Between Ramaswamy and Acton, Plus Voter ID Amendment
events.summary: Ohio's Nov. 3, 2026 ballot featured an open-seat governor's race between Republican Vivek Ramaswamy and Democrat Amy Acton, former state health director, with pre-election polling showing Acton leading by roughly 5 points. Ohio Issue 3, a GOP-backed constitutional amendment enshrining the state's photo voter ID requirement, also appeared on the ballot.

events.headline: Armenian PM Pashinyan Accuses Russia-Linked Circles of Backing Opposition Plot Amid Parliament Brawl
events.summary: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan accused circles linked to Russia and the Eurasian Economic Union of backing a secret opposition plot against his government. The allegations coincided with a physical brawl in Armenia's parliament.

events.headline: Missouri Storm System Shifts to Flash-Flood Risk as Rivers Forecast to Crest Near Maryville
events.summary: A storm system that brought a severe-weather and tornado threat to northwest Missouri and northeast Kansas dropped 1-3 inches of rain around Nov. 2-3, 2026, prompting NWS hydrologic outlooks for rising rivers across Missouri, Iowa, and Nebraska. The 102 River at Maryville, Missouri (flood stage 18.0 ft) was forecast to crest near 18.5 feet by the morning of Nov. 4.

events.headline: New Jersey Governor Warns Ports Against Accepting Russian Diesel Shipments
events.summary: Gov. Mikie Sherrill sent letters to roughly a dozen New Jersey port and terminal operators warning them to turn away tankers carrying Russian diesel, arguing a recent Treasury license conflicts with the 2022 federal ban on Russian oil-product imports. She warned operators could face civil or criminal penalties for accepting the shipments.

events.headline: Taiwan Accuses China of APEC Protocol Violation Over Emailed Shenzhen Summit Invitation
events.summary: Taiwan accused China of violating APEC protocol by sending an emailed invitation to a Shenzhen summit in a manner Taipei said was designed to diminish its status. The dispute adds to ongoing friction between Taiwan and China over diplomatic recognition.

events.headline: NSW Health Declares 'Major Incident' Over Cyber Breach, Launches Criminal Investigation
events.summary: New South Wales Health declared a major incident after a cyber breach exposed sensitive data, prompting a criminal investigation into suspected overseas hackers. Authorities are working to assess the scope of compromised patient records.

events.headline: Washington Voters Decide Income-Tax Repeal and Transgender-Sports Ballot Initiatives
events.summary: Washington voters on Nov. 3, 2026 decided Initiative 645, which would repeal the state's newly enacted 9.9% income tax on earnings over $1 million, and Initiative 638, which would ban transgender girls from K-12 girls' school sports. The election also determined all 98 state House seats and 24 of 49 Senate seats.

events.headline: Jordan Intercepts 14 Armed Individuals Crossing From Syria
events.summary: Jordanian forces stopped a group of 14 armed individuals attempting to cross from Syria into Mafraq Governorate on Oct 30-31, exchanging fire that killed some while others fled back across the border. The incident follows earlier Jordanian strikes on Syria after a deadly church attack in Jordan.

events.headline: Five Charged in $235 Million Fraud Scheme Targeting Australia's NDIS and Welfare Payments
events.summary: Australian Federal Police charged five people over an alleged $235 million fraud scheme targeting the National Disability Insurance Scheme, childcare subsidies and veterans' payments. The operation highlights ongoing concerns about fraud within Australia's welfare system.

events.headline: Libya's Eastern Parliament Appoints Fawzi Abu Khazam as New Central Bank Governor
events.summary: Libya's eastern-based parliament appointed Fawzi Abu Khazam as the new governor of the central bank, accepting the resignation of his predecessor. The move caps a series of recent changes to Libya's financial leadership amid ongoing political division between eastern and western authorities.

events.headline: Bomb Threats Disrupt Multiple Flights Across Poland, Spain and Bulgaria
events.summary: A wave of bomb threats forced the evacuation and diversion of several flights across Europe, including in Warsaw, Spain and Bulgaria. No explosives were found, and authorities are investigating the source of the coordinated threats.

events.headline: Anthrax Outbreak Kills Nearly 30 Hippos in DR Congo's Virunga National Park
events.summary: Bacillus anthracis has killed approximately 28-30 hippos along the Semuliki River in Virunga National Park over the past month, prompting zoonotic-risk warnings for nearby communities.

events.headline: Wes Moore Wins Second Term as Maryland Governor in Landslide
events.summary: Democrat Wes Moore defeated Republican Dan Cox by about 29 points, roughly 62.6%-33%, in a rematch of their 2022 race; Lt. Gov. Aruna Miller was also re-elected. Moore now faces a projected $3 billion state budget shortfall in his second term.

events.headline: Bangladesh Garment Workers Continue Multi-Day Wage Protests; Government Forms Wage Board
events.summary: Garment workers in Bangladesh continued wage protests for a third consecutive day, disrupting factory operations in Dhaka and Gazipur. The government responded by announcing the formation of a wage board to address worker demands.

events.headline: Amy Klobuchar Elected Minnesota's First Female Governor
events.summary: US Sen. Amy Klobuchar (D) defeated Minnesota House Speaker Lisa Demuth (R) roughly 57%-43% in the open-seat race after Gov. Tim Walz declined to seek a third term. Klobuchar becomes Minnesota's first female governor.

events.headline: Fiji Military Formally Backs Removing Constitutional Coup-Immunity Provisions
events.summary: Fiji's military formally declared its support for removing coup-immunity provisions from the constitution, pledging political neutrality. The move comes as Fiji's parliament has delayed a vote on the constitutional amendment bill to December.

events.headline: Serbia Marks Second Anniversary of Novi Sad Canopy Collapse Amid Political Transition
events.summary: Thousands marched in Novi Sad on Nov 1 and held 16 minutes of silence for the 16 victims of the 2024 railway station canopy collapse, a week after the Students' List movement won parliamentary elections over President Vucic's SNS party. Thirteen officials, including a former minister, remain under prosecution.

events.headline: Marsha Blackburn Elected Tennessee's First Woman Governor
events.summary: US Sen. Marsha Blackburn (R) won a narrower-than-expected race over Democrat Jerri Green to become Tennessee's first female governor. Voters also approved amendments expanding courts' ability to deny bail in certain violent-crime cases and permanently banning a state property tax.

events.headline: Former East Aurora School Board President Indicted in $1.3M Kickback Scheme
events.summary: Annette Johnson, former president of East Aurora School District 131's board, was federally indicted over allegedly steering a $2.7 million COVID-relief air-purifier contract to a vendor who funneled over $1 million as commission to a company owned by her boyfriend, where she worked as CFO. Aurora's mayor said a broader review found roughly $43 million flowed from the district to companies linked to Johnson between 2018-2023; Johnson denies wrongdoing.

events.headline: USDA Confirms New World Screwworm in Arizona Dog, Third US State Hit by Outbreak
events.summary: USDA APHIS confirmed New World screwworm, a flesh-eating parasitic fly, in a dog in Cochise County, Arizona, on Oct. 28, 2026, the state's first case in roughly six decades and the third US state after Texas and New Mexico to report one in the current outbreak. Officials established a 20-km infested zone with animal-movement controls and increased surveillance and trapping.

events.headline: French Students Blockade Schools Ahead of November 5 Nationwide Strike
events.summary: Students blockaded dozens of schools and universities across France ahead of a planned nationwide strike on November 5. The protests add pressure on the government amid an already tense political and budgetary standoff in Paris.

events.headline: Seven Arrested in Cross-Border Investment-Fraud Crackdown Across Kosovo, Albania and North Macedonia
events.summary: Authorities across Kosovo, Albania and North Macedonia, coordinated by Eurojust, dismantled an international investment-fraud scheme and arrested seven people. Servers used to run the scheme were also seized.

events.headline: Egypt and Sudan Reaffirm Defense and Water-Security Pact, Reject Unilateral GERD Actions
events.summary: Egypt and Sudan reaffirmed a defense and water-security agreement, jointly rejecting unilateral actions in the Eastern Nile Basin related to the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam. The agreement underscores deepening cooperation between Cairo and Khartoum amid regional tensions over the Nile.

events.headline: Egypt Signs $1 Billion World Bank Financing Agreement for Economic Reform Program
events.summary: Egypt signed a $1 billion financing agreement with the World Bank to support the second phase of its economic reform program. The deal comes as Egypt pursues broader fiscal stabilization measures.

events.headline: Peru's Annual Inflation Hits 5.25%, Highest Since 2023
events.summary: Peru's annual inflation rate rose to 5.25% in October 2026, up from 4.55% in September, marking the eighth consecutive month above the central bank's 1-3% target range. Rising fuel and food prices, exacerbated by El Nino conditions, are driving the increase.

events.headline: Russia Formally Withdraws From Council of Europe Anti-Torture Convention
events.summary: Russia's withdrawal from the European Convention for the Prevention of Torture took effect Nov 1, ending independent monitoring of Russian detention facilities by the Council of Europe's CPT committee.

events.headline: Gabon's President Oligui Nguema Begins State Visit to China
events.summary: Gabonese President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema began a state visit to China on Nov 3 at President Xi Jinping's invitation, running through Nov 7. Afreximbank separately forecasts Gabon's 2026 GDP growth accelerating to 3.3%.

events.headline: Ecuador Imposes Fourth Coastal Curfew of 2026 Ahead of Nov 29 Local Elections
events.summary: Ecuador's government imposed its fourth curfew of the year across five coastal provinces (Guayas, Manabi, Los Rios, El Oro, Esmeraldas) from Nov 1-10, resulting in 218 arrests, ahead of Nov 29 local elections. The move follows the Oct 22 arrest of opposition leader Luisa Gonzalez on campaign-finance allegations, which her party calls politically motivated.

events.headline: Lebanese Delegation Holds Talks With Syria on Refugees and Border Security
events.summary: A Lebanese ministerial delegation led by Deputy PM Tarek Mitri met Syrian Foreign Minister al-Shaibani in Damascus on Nov 2, discussing refugee returns, border security, prisoners and anti-trafficking cooperation.

events.headline: Brazil Summons Argentine Envoy Over Flávio Bolsonaro's Escape to the US via Argentina
events.summary: Brazil's government formally summoned Argentina's diplomatic representative to explain how Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, left Brazil and traveled to the United States via Argentina. Argentina has not confirmed whether it assisted his departure, deepening a diplomatic rift between the two countries.

events.headline: Trial Begins for Suspect in Deadly Leipzig Car-Ramming Attack
events.summary: The trial of the suspect accused of carrying out a deadly car-ramming attack in Leipzig, Germany, began this week. A judge had previously ordered the suspect to undergo psychiatric evaluation.

events.headline: Al-Shabaab Mortar Attack Kills Civilians Near Bosaso, Puntland
events.summary: An al-Shabaab mortar attack killed at least three civilians and wounded seven others near Galgala in Puntland, Somalia. The attack is separate from a recent large-scale al-Shabaab ambush in Lower Shabelle.

events.headline: Thailand Reaffirms Cambodia Border Will Stay Closed Indefinitely
events.summary: Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said the border with Cambodia would remain closed indefinitely, ruling out a return to normal relations for now. The closure continues to disrupt cross-border trade and travel between the two countries.

events.headline: Cyclone Wati Strikes Cook Islands as Unusually Early First Named Storm of Season
events.summary: Tropical Cyclone Wati struck the Cook Islands, including Aitutaki, as the season's first named cyclone, forming unusually early. Authorities issued warnings as the system tracked south toward open waters.

events.headline: Delhi's Air Quality Deteriorates to 'Very Poor,' GRAP Stage II Curbs Invoked
events.summary: New Delhi's air quality worsened to 'very poor' levels, with the AQI climbing to 331, prompting authorities to invoke Stage II of the Graded Response Action Plan. The curbs include restrictions aimed at controlling pollution sources across the capital region.

events.headline: Argentina's Country-Risk Index Surpasses 800 Points, Highest in Over a Year
events.summary: JP Morgan's EMBI country-risk index for Argentina closed at 803 points on Nov 2, having touched 805 intraday, its highest level in more than a year. The spike reflects investor concerns over reserves, debt sustainability and financing conditions.

events.headline: Italy Issues Orange Alert for Storms and Flash Flooding in Puglia and Basilicata
events.summary: Italy's Civil Protection department issued an orange weather alert for Puglia and Basilicata on Nov 2-3 due to intense thunderstorms and flash-flood risk linked to a weak polar vortex, with yellow alerts issued in five other regions.

events.headline: Greek PM Mitsotakis Unveils 90-Project Reform Plan Ahead of 2027 Election
events.summary: Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis announced a plan of 90 infrastructure, defence, housing and public-service projects, with 26 due by the end of 2026 and 64 by mid-2027, ahead of Greece's spring 2027 election.

events.headline: 36-Hour Shutdown Paralyzes Upper Siang Over Mega Dam Project in Arunachal Pradesh
events.summary: A 36-hour bandh began Nov 2 in Yingkiong, Upper Siang district, disrupting schools, markets and transport, with mobile internet suspended. Protesters are demanding the release of detained activists and a halt to survey work for the proposed 11,200-megawatt Siang Upper hydropower project; the state chief minister has pledged dialogue.

events.headline: Brazil's Ibovespa Stock Index Hits Six-Month Low Ahead of Selic Rate Decision
events.summary: Brazil's benchmark Ibovespa stock index fell to its lowest level in six months as investors positioned ahead of the central bank's upcoming Selic interest-rate decision. The decline reflects growing caution over inflation and fiscal policy in Latin America's largest economy.

events.headline: Drone Strike Hits Ozon Logistics Warehouse in Southern Russia's Adygeysk
events.summary: A drone strike hit a warehouse operated by Russian online retailer Ozon in the town of Adygeysk, in Russia's Republic of Adygea. The incident adds to a growing pattern of drone strikes on logistics and industrial infrastructure deep inside Russian territory.

events.headline: Egypt Retains WHO 'Gold Tier' Status as First Country to Maintain Hepatitis C Elimination Recognition
events.summary: Egypt became the first country worldwide to maintain its WHO 'Gold Tier' status on the path to hepatitis C elimination. The recognition highlights Egypt's sustained public health screening and treatment program.

events.headline: Four Charged Over Planned Farm Attack on Donovan Marx in South Africa
events.summary: South African police charged four people with attempted murder over a planned and premeditated farm attack targeting Donovan Marx near Ventersdorp. The arrests follow a broader pattern of farm attacks drawing national attention in South Africa.
events.locationName: Syferfontein farm, near Ventersdorp, South Africa
